---

### 🌕 **Moon Details:**
- **Altitude:** 12.474° above the horizon  
- **Azimuth:** 241.521° (which is roughly **southwest** direction)  
- **Illumination:** 39.99% (a **waning gibbous** phase)  
- **Distance:** ~388,953 km (which is about 1.25 times the average Earth-Moon distance — so it’s a bit farther than average, but still close enough to be visible with the naked eye)  
- **Sky Conditions:** Bright daylight, clear skies, and good visibility

---

### 🌞 **Sun Details:**
- **Altitude:** 25.288° above the horizon  
- **Azimuth:** 158.346° (which is **southeast** direction)  
- **So the Sun is still up** and the sky is bright daylight — **not nighttime**, but still a good time to observe the Moon.

---

### ✅ **Why You Can See the Moon:**
- **Altitude above horizon:** 12.5° — that’s **just barely above the horizon**, but still visible with the naked eye.  
- **Illumination:** 39.99% — the Moon is **well lit** and not too dark, so it will be visible even in daylight.  
- **Distance:** While the Moon is a bit farther than average, it’s still within the range where it's visible with the naked eye.  
- **Sky Conditions:** Clear skies and bright daylight — you’ll be able to see it, though it may appear **smaller and dimmer** than when it’s closer or more illuminated.

---

### 📍 **Where to Look:**
- The Moon is in the **southwest** direction (azimuth ~241.5°), so you should look toward the **southwest** sky.  
- Since the Sun is in the **southeast**, the Moon is **opposite the Sun**, which is why it's visible in daylight.  
- You might see it **near the horizon**, so be patient and look carefully — especially if there are clouds or bright lights nearby.

---

### 📝 **Tips for Observing:**
- **Look for a bright, white or light gray object** in the southwest sky.  
- The Moon will be **larger than a star**, and **much brighter**.  
- If it’s hard to see, try looking **a few minutes later** — the Moon will rise a bit higher and may be easier to spot.  
- If you have a **pair of binoculars**, you can see more detail, like the **dark mare** (lunar seas) and **bright highlands**.

---

### 📅 **When to Look:**
- You’re already at the right time: **10:45 PST**.  
- The Moon will be visible for a while after this, as it will gradually rise higher in the sky.

---

### ✅ **Conclusion:**
**Yes, you should be able to spot the Moon** with the naked eye from Davis, California, on this date and time. It’s a **waning gibbous** Moon, **well illuminated**, and **visible in daylight**. Just look toward the **southwest** sky and you should see it — especially if the skies are clear and you have a good view of the horizon.
